issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.animals: the UML in the problem statement (Farm class members) declares the field as List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 of the problem statement explicitly requires the aggregation to be realized using a Set implemented with a HashSet. This inconsistency (List vs Set) leaves students unsure which collection type and duplicate semantics (allowing duplicates vs enforcing uniqueness) they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification for Farm.animals. Prefer updating the UML diagram and any UML text to show animals: Set<Animal> (and document HashSet in the textual instructions) so that the problem statement, UML, and expected duplicate behavior all match. Alternatively, if List behavior is intended, change the textual Part 3 to require a List and remove the HashSet mention.

issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.animals in the provided solution uses List<Animal> backed by an ArrayList (private List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>()) while the problem statement's Part 3 requires a Set implemented with a HashSet. The solution's choice changes duplicate-handling semantics and the public API (getter/setter element types) compared with the textual requirement, confusing students about the intended correct implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem statement. Change the solution to declare and initialize the collection as a Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>() and update the getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>. If the exercise intends a List, update the problem statement (Part 3) to remove the HashSet/Set requirement and clarify duplicate behavior.
